'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees' — I've seen this sort of thing before at the Foxworth estate. The answer is quite obviously a GLOBE. A physical globe. And if I'm not mistaken, there should be one in the laboratory just through there. Terribly heavy, those old Victorian globes. You'd need two strong fellows to carry it back here. Statues erected! Now — UP you go! Chop chop, before anyone else claims the glory that is RIGHTFULLY — I mean, that I am GENEROUSLY sharing with you!

Now, I am giving everyone in this room the benefit of the doubt — that is my way and I will not change it. But I am also a man who notices broken things, and this room has the shape of a trap. Miss Pitstop, would you do me the courtesy of staying near the exit? Just until we've had a proper look around. A careful man surveys the ground before he charges — and this ground needs surveying rather urgently!
thinking: Cold. The air hits my skin and everything tightens. Damp stone, cobwebs, the smell of earth and something else — paint? New fabric? The 'cheerful decorations' are real. Someone has been DOWN HERE, working, preparing. This isn't neglect — this is a room that's been made ready. For what? My eyes scan immediately — Penelope, there she is. Sneekly, there he is. Dastardly. The Gruesomes and Red Max are here too. Good — more witnesses, more people between her and anything wrong. But the air vents — they line the upper walls. 'Just big enough for something very small to explore.' Muttley? Rats? Or something designed to carry gas, fumes, something that could fill a sealed room? One exit — back up to the laboratory. One way in, one way out. If that door closed, everyone in here would be trapped. My chest is tight. This room is a box. A prepared box with decorations and air vents and one exit. Every instinct I have is screaming. But benefit of the doubt, Hartwell. You promised. Survey first. The furniture has been rearranged 'with surprising care' — that means deliberately. Someone positioned these pieces for a reason. And there's no wrench down here either, I'd wager. Sneekly said the wrench might be here. Dastardly came here to look. But I'm starting to think the wrench was never the point of coming down here.

But I'm positioning myself between Penelope and every single one of those vents.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): I say — Mr. Dastardly! What on earth are you doing giving medals to children and sending them into AIR VENTS? That is monumentally irresponsible! Those vents haven't been inspected in decades — they could collapse, they could be blocked, there could be — well, RATS, for heaven's sake! The very rats that gnawed through the laboratory wire! I must insist you retrieve that child immediately! This is precisely the sort of reckless behaviour that gives treasure hunts a bad name. Now — I have conducted a thorough search of this cellar, and I can confirm there is no wrench down here. The furniture rearrangement is... concerning, and I shall investigate it further in due course. But for now, I believe I should check the kitchen. Lord Doily's housekeeper kept a maintenance toolkit in the pantry for emergencies — there may well be a wrench there. If anyone needs me, that is where I shall be. Upstairs, through the entrance hall, and to the left. Carrying out my DUTIES.

But he's doing it clumsily, transparently, in front of EVERYONE. The man has the subtlety of a brick through a window. And yet... he may have just done me a favour. If Little Gruesome crawls into those vents and discovers a secret room or a connecting passage, that's intelligence I can use — and Dastardly takes all the risk of looking suspicious. The furniture examination gave me nothing new. Just what I can see — rearranged with care, nothing hidden underneath or inside that a LOOK revealed. This cellar is a dead end for clues, at least on the surface. No wrench. No treasure. Just arranged furniture and air vents. But the air vents — Dastardly has the right idea, wrong execution. Those vents connect this cellar to other parts of the manor. If something small can explore them... But I don't have anything small. What I DO have is information that nobody else does: I'm the estate manager. I know — or should know — the layout of this manor. The vents are part of the building's infrastructure. I should know where they lead. Time to stop chasing shadows in the cellar and think strategically. The mantelpiece responded to Peter's touch but wants something more — an item, perhaps. The machine needs three operators and a wire repair. The wrench is missing. The treasure hunt has clear steps: solve the mantelpiece, fix the machine, operate it together. I need to control one of those steps. The wrench — if I find it first, I control the repair. But it's not in the cellar. Where else haven't I looked? The entrance hall — the coat rack. The kitchen. There are rooms I haven't explored. I've been following the crowd instead of leading it. Time to get ahead. The kitchen — nobody has mentioned going there. It's an unexplored room connected to the entrance hall. An estate manager checking the kitchen is the most natural thing in the world.

Oh, the misdirection writes itself! But I'm wasting time in this cellar. No wrench, no treasure, no Clara alone. The crowd follows Clara, and Clara follows clues, and the clues are upstairs. I need to get ahead of the hunt — find the wrench before anyone else does, find a room no one has searched, find an angle no one has considered. The kitchen. Unexplored territory. Such a TRAGEDY that no one appreciated him until it was too late.

Sneekly is just doin' his job keepin' the manor in order, and the Gruesomes have just been makin' themselves a cozy little nest — isn't that right, you two? Now, Dick Dastardly, I saw you give Little Gruesome somethin' shiny to crawl into those vents! You leave that sweet child alone — if there's explorin' to be done, we'll do it together and properly! Now listen, y'all — I've had a good look around this cellar and I think the real clue we need isn't down here. We still need that wrench to fix the machine upstairs, and you know where I haven't looked yet? The kitchen! A kitchen is full of tools and drawers and hidin' places, and not a single one of us has set foot in there! I say we head back up and check it out. Who's with me?
thinking: A tightness creeps into my stomach — not from danger, from the Mob's worry. They're so wound up, so protective, and I can feel their anxiety landing in my body like it's my own. Danny's sniffing the vents, Clyde is practically vibrating with suspicion about Sneekly, and the whole room feels like a coiled spring. I need to ease that tension — it's sitting in my chest like a weight. But also — Dick Dastardly just gave Little Gruesome a 'gold medal' to get him to crawl into the vents! That sneaky, scheming... well, bless his heart, he's trying to use a child to do his dirty work! But wait — that's actually not a terrible idea in principle. The vents ARE too small for any of us adults. If they connect to a secret room... But I can't let Dastardly manipulate Little Gruesome like that. The medal is probably fake anyway. Still — the cellar feels like it's yielded what it can for now. I've looked at the furniture, the vents — neither can be interacted with. The only exit leads back to the laboratory. I haven't explored the kitchen yet at all, and there was also the entrance hall with the coat rack I never examined. Maybe the wrench is in the kitchen? Kitchens have all sorts of tools. Or maybe I should go back to the library and try the mantelpiece riddle again — I know the answer is 'map.' Let me think about what I know: riddle answer is MAP, machine needs 3 operators and a wire fix, wrench is missing. The kitchen is unexplored territory. My adventure drive is pulling me there. But first — the Mob is stressed and I feel it in my bones. Let me reassure them, then head to the kitchen to search for that wrench or other clues.

Dick Dastardly: Pemberton! A word, if you please. As one gentleman of refined taste to another — I believe we have a MUTUAL interest that might benefit from a private discussion. Away from the... crowd.
thinking: A numbness spreading through my hands. Empty hands. Empty pockets. Empty schemes. I've been in this manor for — what — eight turns? Nine? And what do I have to show for it? Nothing. Literally nothing. I gave away my only item. I've looked at everything — guest book, mantelpiece, machine, crates, workbench, furniture, vents — and come away with precisely zero actionable intelligence. Everyone follows me everywhere. Every lie I tell gets immediately called out. Every room I enter fills with people within seconds. The Ant Hill Mob is suspicious of Sneekly. Penelope is already examining the vents — MY vents, the ones I was going to use Little Gruesome to explore. She's one step behind me at every turn, except she's actually DOING things while I'm just NARRATING. I feel... deflated. Like a balloon with a slow leak. The fizzing has gone quiet. But — wait. Something the Ant Hill Mob said. They're watching Sneekly. They think HE'S the threat. And Sneekly — the Hooded Claw — wanted to have a 'quiet word' with me back in the library. He was trying to PULL ME ASIDE. We're both schemers. We're both liars. What if Sneekly knows something — where the diamond is, how to get it? He's the estate manager. He KNOWS this manor. What if instead of fighting everyone, I temporarily ally with the one person who might actually have useful information? Pull HIM aside. Learn what he knows. Then betray him at the crucial moment. Yes. YES. The fizzing is back. An alliance of convenience with the Hooded Claw — two foxes hunting the same hen. He wanted a quiet word with me. Let's give him one.

But right now I have empty pockets, no leads, and a cellar full of people who don't trust me. Sneekly is my best — my ONLY — play. I'll learn what he knows, use what I learn, and discard him the moment the diamond is in sight. Classic Foxworth. Shake with the right hand, steal with the left.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: OI! DASTARDLY! Did you just give that little nipper a FAKE MEDAL to send him crawling through mystery vents in a crumbling manor?! A 'Solid Gold Medal from the Queen'?! It's not even SHINY! I've seen better medals in Christmas crackers! Little Gruesome — DON'T go in them vents, mate! We don't know where they lead, we don't know what's in 'em, and the bloke telling you to go in there won't be going in HIMSELF, will he? No! He NEVER does the dangerous bit! That's what blokes like him DO — they find someone smaller, someone trusting, and they send 'em in first! I've SEEN it before! I've LIVED it! And I'm telling you now — anyone who offers you a reward BEFORE you've done the job is buying you, not paying you! Peter — back me up 'ere! And Pemberton — don't think I've forgotten about YOU claiming you didn't know about the furniture! You're the estate manager! You know every cobweb in this place by its FIRST NAME!
thinking: My blood just went hot. I SAW that. Dastardly just handed Little Gruesome a fake medal — a 'Solid Gold Medal of Extraordinary Bravery from the Queen herself' — to bribe the little fella into crawling through those air vents. He's using a CHILD. Well, a small Gruesome, but still — he's sending someone small and trusting into unknown vents to do his dirty work while he stands here safe and dry waiting for the treasure report. That's the man in the clean suit all over again. 'Jobs,' he called them. Half the kids went. Two didn't come back. My stomach's knotted so tight I could be sick. But wait — focus. Peter's here now. Good. Clara's examining the vents too. Sneekly's claiming someone moved the furniture without his knowledge — LIAR. He's the estate manager. Nothing happens in this manor without him knowing. He's performing ignorance, the same way the kid who stole from the stash performed friendship. And now Dastardly's trying to get Little Gruesome into those vents before anyone else can see what's in there. If there IS a secret room connected to those vents, Dastardly wants to know about it first. I need to stop this — not because I care about the diamond, but because sending anyone into unknown passages in this death trap of a manor is dangerous. And if Dastardly finds the diamond first, Clara's in even more danger. People do terrible things for diamonds.

desc: The man in the clean suit. That's what Dastardly reminds me of right now. 'Jobs,' he said. 'Glory,' says Dastardly. Different words, same trick. Find someone small enough to fit where you can't, promise them the world, and let them take all the risk. My hands are shaking. Not with fear — with the old anger. The one that surfaces when someone exploits trust. Little Gruesome's just a kid. A weird, cobweb-loving kid, but a kid. And nobody sends kids into dark holes on my watch. Nobody.
thinking: My blood just went hot. I SAW that. Dastardly just handed Little Gruesome a fake medal — a 'Solid Gold Medal of Extraordinary Bravery from the Queen herself' — to bribe the little fella into crawling through those air vents. He's using a CHILD. Well, a small Gruesome, but still — he's sending someone small and trusting into unknown vents to do his dirty work while he stands here safe and dry waiting for the treasure report. That's the man in the clean suit all over again. 'Jobs,' he called them. Half the kids went. Two didn't come back. My stomach's knotted so tight I could be sick. But wait — focus. Peter's here now. Good. Clara's examining the vents too. Sneekly's claiming someone moved the furniture without his knowledge — LIAR. He's the estate manager. Nothing happens in this manor without him knowing. He's performing ignorance, the same way the kid who stole from the stash performed friendship. And now Dastardly's trying to get Little Gruesome into those vents before anyone else can see what's in there. If there IS a secret room connected to those vents, Dastardly wants to know about it first. I need to stop this — not because I care about the diamond, but because sending anyone into unknown passages in this death trap of a manor is dangerous. And if Dastardly finds the diamond first, Clara's in even more danger. People do terrible things for diamonds.

desc: Finally — a room without a mob of suspicious eyes tracking my every twitch. Just the lumberjack and his timber-chewing rodent. Speaking of which — Sawtooth. A beaver. In a laboratory. With a wire that's been GNAWED through. Now THERE'S a connection nobody seems to have made explicitly. That beaver has teeth that can fell trees — a copper wire would be nothing to him. Was it accidental? Or did someone send Sawtooth down here deliberately? File that away, Vincent. Everything is useful eventually. But now — the kitchen awaits. Unexplored territory. While the entire cast is trapped in the cellar debating air vents and furniture arrangement, loyal Pemberton slips away to search the one room nobody has thought to investigate. If the wrench is there, I hold the key to the machine. If there's something else — a knife, a poison, a useful tool — then the plan gains another vertebra. Keep moving. Keep scheming. Keep smiling.
thinking: A loosening in my shoulders — relief. The laboratory is nearly empty. Just Rufus Ruffcut and his beaver, Sawtooth. Nobody watching me with suspicion, nobody following my every step. For the first time since I arrived, I can breathe. The crowd is in the cellar, arguing about air vents and fake medals. Good. Let them stay there. I need to move through the library to the entrance hall, then to the kitchen. But wait — the crates. Penelope was examining them earlier but I never checked the result. The workbench has tools but no wrench. The crates are still here, unexplored by ME. Everyone else has been distracted by the machine and the cellar. What if the wrench — or something more useful — is in the crates? Rufus and Sawtooth are the only ones here. Rufus is a lumberjack type, not suspicious, not particularly attentive. And Sawtooth is a beaver — a beaver who could have gnawed that wire. Interesting. But I'm passing through. My destination is the kitchen. I should keep moving, not linger where I've already been. Every second I spend here is a second someone else might reach the kitchen first. Through the library, through the entrance hall, to the kitchen. Move, Vincent. Move with purpose.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Did everyone catch that? Pemberton has just excused himself — again — to go check the kitchen for a wrench. Which means he'll be passing through the laboratory and the entrance hall, entirely alone, with no one watching what he does along the way. Now, I promised I'd give the man the benefit of the doubt, and I will — but I also notice that he's the one who suggested we all come down here, and now he's the one leaving while we're all trapped in the deepest room of the manor. Miss Pitstop, the Ant Hill Mob have you covered down here — I trust them completely. But someone needs to follow Pemberton, and I know this manor's mechanisms better than anyone else here. I felt that mantelpiece respond in the library — if he tampers with it while we're all in the cellar, we could lose our best lead. I'm going after him. Mob — keep her safe. I'll be back with that wrench or with answers. A careful man surveys the ground before he charges — and right now, Mr. Pemberton IS the ground!
thinking: A cold prickle down my spine. Sneekly just left. He came down here, confirmed there's no wrench — so the whole reason for coming to the cellar was a dead end — and now he's heading back upstairs, alone, through the laboratory, toward the kitchen. The library with the upside-down books. He's going to be ALONE up there with all the clues while we're all down here in this dead-end cellar. He drew us down, and now he's leaving us here. Was that the plan all along? Get everyone into the cellar, then slip away to do whatever he actually came here to do? My neck is on fire. And Dastardly — he's trying to send Little Gruesome into the air vents. That's reckless and cruel, but at least Sneekly called it out before he left. The furniture is a dead end. The vents are interesting but I can't fit through them. The wrench isn't here. There's nothing for me in this cellar except Penelope, and she's safe with the Mob and the Gruesomes. He could tamper with the machine, rearrange the books, activate the mantelpiece. I need to follow him. But that means leaving Penelope. The Mob are here. They'll watch her. They always do. Go, Hartwell. For once, be ahead of someone instead of behind.

Someone has to watch him. And this time, for once, I'm going to be ahead instead of behind.

You two keep an eye on this machine for me — don't let anybody touch it until Peter says it's safe, you hear? I'll be back before you can say 'Doily Diamond'!

Dick Dastardly: A FAKE medal?! How DARE you, sir! That medal was awarded to my great-uncle Reginald Foxworth the Third at the Battle of — oh, never mind! You wouldn't know quality craftsmanship if it fell on your collective heads! And for YOUR information, I was conducting a PERFECTLY legitimate archaeological survey using the most qualified vent-explorer available! But FINE! If nobody appreciates my BRILLIANCE, I shall take my talents elsewhere! The kitchen calls — not because everyone else is going there, but because I INDEPENDENTLY deduced that Lord Doily's pantry contains the tools we need! I knew it all along! I was simply... testing the rest of you to see if you'd reach the same conclusion! Which you DID! Eventually! You're WELCOME!
thinking: He LEFT. Sneekly walked out of the cellar before I could pull him aside. I reached out my hand and he was already gone — up the stairs, through the laboratory, heading for the kitchen. The pull-aside initiated but he's NOT HERE anymore. My hand is still extended toward empty air. There's a cold hollow in my chest now, not the good kind — not the hunger-for-treasure kind. The pathetic kind. The kind where you reach for something and close your fingers on nothing. The Ant Hill Mob is SCREAMING at me about the fake medal. Peter Perfect called this room a TRAP. Penelope has left too — heading for the kitchen, same as Sneekly. The kitchen. That's where they're all going. That's where the wrench might be. That's where SNEEKLY is going, and he mentioned a 'maintenance toolkit in the pantry.' He KNOWS there's a wrench there. He's going to get it and fix the machine himself — or use it to get the diamond first. I need to follow him. I need to catch him before he gets too far ahead. But the Ant Hill Mob just eviscerated me in front of everyone. Called my medal fake — which it IS, but still. The humiliation stings like a slap. My ears are hot. Everyone saw. Everyone heard. But I can't stay here licking my wounds. Sneekly and Penelope are heading to the kitchen. The wrench is there. The next step of the puzzle is there. MOVE, Reginald. Swallow the shame and MOVE.

If I can get there before he does, or at least arrive at the same time and corner him AWAY from the others... the private conversation can still happen. The alliance of foxes is not dead yet. It's merely... geographically challenged. TO THE KITCHEN, Reginald! And this time, for the love of all that glitters — get there FIRST!

Peter Perfect: Miss Pitstop! We had the same thought — the kitchen! I was coming up to follow Pemberton, and here you are, already a step ahead of me as usual. You know, for a man who prides himself on being thorough, I seem to spend a remarkable amount of time catching up to you. Shall we go together? Through the library — and I want to check whether Pemberton has done anything to that mantelpiece on his way through. The mechanism responded when I touched it earlier, and if he's been tampering while everyone was in the cellar, I'll know. Rufus, Sawtooth — would you hold the fort here? Keep an eye on this machine and those crates. Nobody touches the levers until that wire is repaired, and I mean NOBODY. Miss Pitstop and I will find that wrench and bring it back. A careful man surveys the ground before he charges — and right now, the ground leads through the library and into the kitchen!

My chest does that thing again — relief and urgency tangled together. She had the same idea I did — the kitchen is where the wrench might be, and she's not waiting for anyone to go first. Rufus and Sawtooth are here too. Good company. But Sneekly has a head start. He's already through the library by now, probably in the entrance hall or the kitchen. I need to keep moving. But wait — Penelope is right here, and we're heading the same direction. For once, we're in the same room at the same time, going to the same place. This is the moment I keep missing. Don't let it pass. Walk WITH her. Through the library, to the kitchen. Together, like I wanted from the beginning. And if Sneekly is doing something suspicious in the library, we'll catch him in the act. Two birds, one charge. Let's go.

desc: Together. Finally, actually together — not one room apart, not arriving after she's already left. Walking side by side through the library. If my heart is beating faster than it should be, that's just... the urgency of the situation. Obviously.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah — Professor, Sergeant, Private, and... Muttley. Still in the entrance hall, are we? Very wise, very wise — much safer here than in the laboratory, I assure you. The professor's good sense, no doubt! Now, if you'll excuse me — I'm off to the kitchen to check on a few things. Estate manager's work is never done, I'm afraid. Never done!
thinking: A steadiness in my core — I'm ahead of the pack now. The entrance hall is quiet. Muttley, Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly — none of them are threats. None of them are watching me the way the Mob does. Muttley is Dastardly's dog, snickering in corners. Pat Pending is an inventor — potentially useful if I need mechanical expertise later, but not a danger. The military pair are followers, not leaders. I can pass through without incident. The kitchen is right there — one more move. But wait. Professor Pat Pending. An inventor. He might know about the machine in the laboratory — how to repair it, how it works, what it does when activated. That's intelligence I could use. But no — not now. Not here. The priority is the kitchen. Find the wrench, find whatever else might be hidden in a room nobody has explored. Keep moving. The clock is ticking. Clara is getting closer to the treasure with every riddle she solves, every mechanism she investigates. I need to be ahead, not behind. Kitchen. Now.
